The test `test_failure()` checks whether an empty task with `fail=True` is successfully executed by the `Worker`. However, this test failed due to an assertion error that lists differ. Upon inspecting the execution path, we find that the task `EmptyTask(fail=True)` is not handled correctly in the `run` method of the `luigi.worker.Worker` class. Specifically, when a task is executed without any custom `complete()` method and fails (due to its `fail=True` attribute), it does not trigger an exception or other special handling within the loop that executes tasks.

This discrepancy leads to the task being incorrectly reported as successfully executed, despite its fail state.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

luigi.worker.Worker._run_task(EmptyTask) 
luigi.worker.Worker._handle_next_task() 

Note: I assumed that the issue is in the task execution and handling within the loop of the `Worker.run` method. Therefore, I identified two methods that are likely to be responsible for the bug.
